name: Discrete Leibniz product rule for Z-valued sequences

statement.latest: For Z-valued sequences f, g and a finite-difference operator Delta, the discrete Leibniz product rule Delta(f*g)(n) = f(n+1)*Delta g(n) + Delta f(n)*g(n) holds exactly with no remainder term.

reverification_2026-09-08.evidence: Original proposal bundled the discrete FTC (FTC, FTC_Z, FTC_inverse) with the discrete Leibniz product rule. The FTC part is a DUPLICATE: A2/M.03.v1 ('ftcc_Z', tier Th_coqc, coq_status closed) proves `fold Z.add 0 (zdelta f) N = f N - f 0` and Z/M.06.v1 ('FTCC_telescope', tier Th_coqc, coq_status closed) proves `Agg f N == f N - f 0` -- both are the identical telescoping-sum-recovers-endpoint-difference identity URCF states as FTC/FTC_Z/FTC_inverse (renaming Sum/Delta for Agg/zdelta, same object under the phi-criterion). The Leibniz part is GENUINELY NEW: it is a pointwise per-step identity (Delta of a product at one step n), logically distinct from Z/M.09.v1 ('summation_by_parts', tier Th_coqc, coq_status closed), which is the SUMMED/telescoped consequence over a whole range [0,N] -- summation_by_parts implies but does not state the pointwise Leibniz rule, and no reading states the pointwise rule directly. This proposal is trimmed to keep only the Leibniz content; the FTC content is dropped as a duplicate of A2/M.03.v1 and Z/M.06.v1.
reverification_2026-09-08.corroborates: URCF's FTC/FTC_Z/FTC_inverse proofs (over the D-derived Zr type) are an independently-authored second proof route for the same telescoping identity A2/M.03.v1 and Z/M.06.v1 already establish over Coq's stdlib Z -- worth a second_proof-style note on those two entries if the founder wants it (field does not exist yet in registry/SCHEMA.md; flagged, not invented).

name: R (Bishop regular Cauchy sequences of Q) is a complete constructive ordered field

statement.latest: R := Bishop regular Cauchy sequences of Q with equality Req and injection inj_Q; R is an ordered field up to Req (Radd/Rle/Rlt/Rmul group, order and ring laws), Cauchy-complete (R_complete, R_complete_metric) with a constructive lattice (Rmax/Rmin), a convergence relation (Rconv), inverses (Rinv/Rinv_gen), a metric (Rdist) and basic epsilon-delta continuity (Rcontinuous_at) -- the top rung of the discrete-root number ladder D -> Z -> Q -> R.

reverification_2026-09-08.evidence: Root R's prose already asserts the ordered-field + Cauchy-completeness claim (Th 3.5/3.6) verbatim. Checked all 40 R/* readings: R/M.33.v1 (radd_at), R/M.34.v1 (rmul_at), R/M.35.v1 (radd_comm), R/M.36.v1 (const_gap_zero) and R/M.37.v1 (gap_subadditive), origin coq/information-discrete-math formal/IDM_Continuum.v, DO give a thin pre-existing partial witness for a DIFFERENT representation of R: pointwise sequences g,h:nat->Q with a generic 'gap' modulus function, only proving pointwise add/mul definitions and commutativity of add plus subadditivity of the gap function -- narrower and structurally different from URCF's Bishop-regular-Cauchy-sequence construction (explicit 1/n+1/m modulus, Req equivalence, inj_Q injection). Under the phi-criterion this thin overlap (radd_comm-type triviality) is arguably the same trivial fact re-proved on a different concrete representation, so it is flagged as an overlap rather than ignored. The remaining, overwhelming majority of URCF's claim -- the FULL order (Rle/Rlt, antisymmetry, cotransitivity), the multiplicative inverse (Rinv/Rinv_gen), Cauchy-completeness (R_complete, R_complete_metric), the lattice (Rmax/Rmin), convergence (Rconv, uniqueness of limits), the metric (Rdist, triangle inequality, Lipschitz properties) and basic continuity (Rcontinuous_at) -- has NO existing reading anywhere in CANONICAL.json (confirmed via keyword search: 'positive semidefinite'-style scan for order/completeness/metric/convergence terms restricted to R/* returned only the thin radd/rmul/gap family above). Kept as partial_overlap rather than trimmed, since the overlapping piece (a near-trivial pointwise-add-commutativity fact on a structurally different representation) is a small fraction of the object and stripping it would lose the coherent field+completeness package; the reviewer should weigh whether the R/M.33-37 family and this proposal are close enough kin to eventually cross-reference at merge time.
